{
  "verdict": "fix",
  "issues": [
    "The GET /tasks endpoint lacks pagination, which will cause severe performance and memory issues as the dataset grows.",
    "The PUT /tasks/{id} endpoint uses optional fields for partial updates, which violates standard REST semantics where PUT is intended for full resource replacement.",
    "The API contract completely omits error response definitions (e.g., 400, 404, 500) and their payload structures, leaving clients without a standardized way to handle failures.",
    "Replacing OpenAPI with a proprietary custom JSON format sacrifices standard tooling, code generation, and validation, creating unnecessary friction for client integration."
  ],
  "suggestions": [
    "Implement pagination (e.g., limit/offset or cursor-based) for the GET /tasks endpoint to handle large datasets safely.",
    "Change the update endpoint to PATCH for partial updates, or explicitly define PUT to require the full resource representation.",
    "Define a standard error response schema (including status codes and error message structures) for all endpoints.",
    "Consider using a minimal OpenAPI 3.0 specification or JSON Schema instead of a custom format to maintain industry-standard tooling compatibility."
  ]
}
